question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|7y+3|=7y+3,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|7y+3| & =1 \\ 7y+3 & =1 \\ 7y & =-2 \\ \frac{7y}{7} & =\frac{-2}{7} \\ y & =-\frac{2}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|7y+3|=-(7y+3),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|7y+3| & =1 \\ -(7y+3) & =1 \\ -7y-3 & =1 \\ -7y & =4 \\ \frac{-7y}{-7} & =\frac{4}{-7} \\ y & =-\frac{4}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=-\frac{4}{7}$ and $y=-\frac{2}{7}.$
